question:
Read the below statement:

1. The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 76 of the Constitution.

2. A candidate contesting an election to the Lok Sabha is required to make a security deposit of Rs. 25,000.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both statements 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 76. He must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court, is the highest law officer of the country, and holds office during the pleasure of the President. (महान्यायवादी — अनुच्छेद 76)

 

• The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India, and the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament and their committees, without the right to vote (Article 88). He is not a member of the Cabinet and is permitted private legal practice, subject to restrictions.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate for the Lok Sabha must deposit Rs. 25,000, reduced to Rs. 12,500 for a candidate belonging to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. For a State Legislative Assembly the amounts are Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 5,000 respectively. The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure more than one-sixth of the valid votes polled.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Solicitor General of India and the Additional Solicitors General assist the Attorney General, but they are appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, not by the President, and their office finds no mention in the Constitution.

 

• For the office of President of India, a candidate must make a security deposit of Rs. 15,000 and the nomination must be subscribed by at least 50 proposers and 50 seconders from among the electors.

 

• The corresponding State-level officer is the Advocate General, appointed by the Governor under Article 165.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question:
Based on the given statements which option is correct:

Statement I: The Gandhara school of art shows a strong Greco-Roman influence in its images of the Buddha.

Statement II: The Gandhara school used white marble as its principal medium of sculpture.
option_1: Statement I and II both are Correct
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statement I is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct. The Gandhara school, which flourished in the north-west under the Kushanas, especially Kanishka, shows a marked Greco-Roman (Hellenistic) influence. Its Buddha images have wavy hair, sharp features, a well-formed forehead, and heavy drapery falling in realistic folds, resembling the Roman toga. It is therefore also called the Indo-Greek or Graeco-Buddhist school. (गांधार शैली — यूनानी-रोमन प्रभाव)

 

• Statement II is incorrect. The Gandhara school used grey sandstone and blue-grey schist, along with stucco. It was the Amaravati school of the Satavahanas, in the lower Krishna valley, that used white marble.

 

• The three great schools of ancient Indian sculpture:

◦ Gandhara — north-west; grey sandstone/schist; Greco-Roman influence; Buddha shown with a halo without ornamentation

◦ Mathura — Uttar Pradesh; spotted red sandstone; entirely indigenous; it produced images for both Indian and non-Indian patrons and freely used nature-based themes such as trees, animals and yakshis

◦ Amaravati — Andhra Pradesh; white marble; narrative panels of the Buddha's life, with slender, graceful figures

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Buddha was first depicted in human form under the Kushanas, at Gandhara and Mathura. In the earlier art of Bharhut and Sanchi, he was shown only through symbols — the lotus, the wheel, the bodhi tree, the footprint and the empty throne.

 

• The Mathura school also produced the famous headless statue of Kanishka, and images of Jain Tirthankaras and Hindu deities, showing that it served several faiths.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Statement II wrongly names the medium used by the Gandhara school.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Statement I is factually accurate.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Statement I is correct, so it cannot be that neither is correct.

question: Which of the following statements about the Pushkar Fair of Rajasthan is correct?
option_1: It is a boat race festival held on the backwaters during the monsoon
option_2: It is celebrated only by women of Jaisalmer through crafts and songs
option_3: It marks the onset of the monsoon and the sowing of kharif crops
option_4: It is an annual livestock and camel fair held at Pushkar in Ajmer district around Kartik Purnima
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is an annual livestock and camel fair held at Pushkar in Ajmer district around Kartik Purnima.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela) is held every year at Pushkar in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, in the month of Kartik (October-November), culminating on Kartik Purnima. (पुष्कर मेला — अजमेर, राजस्थान)

 

• It is one of the largest camel and livestock fairs in the world, at which camels, horses and cattle are traded, alongside competitions such as camel races, the "longest moustache" contest and matka phod.

 

• It is simultaneously a religious fair: pilgrims take a holy dip in the Pushkar Lake, and the town has one of the very few temples in India dedicated to Lord Brahma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important fairs and festivals:

◦ Hola Mohalla — Punjab, at Anandpur Sahib, held the day after Holi; started by Guru Gobind Singh in 1701, it showcases martial arts (gatka), Nihang mock battles and langars

◦ Sonepur Mela — Bihar, on Kartik Purnima, Asia's largest cattle fair

◦ Kumbh Mela — Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik

◦ Surajkund Crafts Mela — Haryana

◦ Nauchandi Mela — Meerut, Uttar Pradesh

◦ Baneshwar Fair — Dungarpur, Rajasthan, the fair of the tribals

 

• Other major Rajasthani festivals are Teej, Gangaur, Marwar Festival and the Desert Festival at Jaisalmer.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Boat races on the backwaters describe the Nehru Trophy Boat Race of Kerala, held during Onam.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The Pushkar Fair is attended by people of all communities and is above all a livestock fair.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: It falls in October-November, after the monsoon, not at its onset.

question: In ancient Indian music theory, the term 'Desi Sangita' referred to music that was:
option_1: Rooted in the regional and folk traditions of a particular area
option_2: Derived strictly from the Vedic chants and sacrificial ritual
option_3: Composed exclusively in Sanskrit for temple worship
option_4: Introduced into India through contact with Persia and Central Asia
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rooted in the regional and folk traditions of a particular area.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ancient Indian musical theory, systematised in Matanga's Brihaddeshi (about the 8th century CE) and in Sharngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara (13th century), divides music into two broad streams: (मार्गी एवं देशी संगीत)

◦ Margi Sangita — literally "of the path"; music rooted in the Vedic traditions, governed by fixed rules, sung for spiritual merit and liberation. It was regarded as sacred, unchanging and divine in origin.

◦ Desi Sangita — literally "of the region"; music rooted in the regional and folk traditions of a particular area, shaped by local taste and language, composed for the pleasure of ordinary people, and free to change.

 

• Over time it was the Desi stream, being flexible and living, that developed into the raga-based classical music of India, while the Margi tradition survives chiefly in Vedic chanting (samagana).

 

• The Samaveda is regarded as the fountainhead of Indian music, and Bharata's Natyashastra is the earliest comprehensive treatise on music, dance and drama.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sharngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara is called the "Ocean of Music" and is honoured in both the Hindustani and the Carnatic traditions, since it was written before the two streams diverged.

 

• Indian classical music divided into the Hindustani and Carnatic systems from about the 13th to 14th centuries, largely as a result of Persian and Central Asian influence in the north.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Music derived from Vedic tradition and ritual is Margi Sangita, the counterpart of Desi.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Desi music was composed in regional languages, which is precisely what distinguished it.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Foreign influence shaped later Hindustani music, but the Margi-Desi distinction is far older and internal to Indian theory.

question: In wrestling, the term 'fall' (pin) refers to which of the following?
option_1: Deliberately stepping outside the boundary of the mat
option_2: A caution given to a wrestler for passivity
option_3: Holding both shoulders of the opponent down on the mat for the required time, which ends the bout immediately
option_4: Winning the bout on the basis of accumulated technical points
solution_text:
The correct answer is Holding both shoulders of the opponent down on the mat for the required time, which ends the bout immediately.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A fall, also called a pin, occurs when a wrestler holds both shoulders (scapulae) of the opponent in contact with the mat long enough for the referee to observe control. A fall gives an immediate victory and the bout ends at once, whatever the score. (फॉल या पिन — तत्काल विजय)

 

• Other ways of winning a wrestling bout are victory by technical superiority (a lead of 10 points in freestyle and 8 points in Greco-Roman), victory on points at the end of regulation time, victory by injury or default, and disqualification.

 

• Points are awarded for takedowns, exposure (turning the opponent's back to the mat), reversals and for pushing the opponent out of the mat area. Deliberately fleeing the mat or the hold and illegal holds are penalised.

 

• The two Olympic styles are freestyle, in which the whole body may be used and the legs may be attacked, and Greco-Roman, in which holds below the waist are forbidden.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The world governing body is United World Wrestling (UWW), headquartered at Corsier-sur-Vevey, Switzerland. A wrestling bout is contested over two periods of three minutes with a 30-second break.

 

• India's Olympic wrestling medallists include K.D. Jadhav (bronze, Helsinki 1952 — India's first individual Olympic medal), Sushil Kumar, Yogeshwar Dutt, Sakshi Malik, Ravi Dahiya, Bajrang Punia and Aman Sehrawat.

 

• Traditional Indian wrestling is called Kushti or Pehlwani, practised in an earthen pit called an akhara, and the Hind Kesari and Bharat Kesari are its best-known titles.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Leaving the mat deliberately is fleeing, which is penalised with a point to the opponent.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: A caution for passivity is a warning, not a fall.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Winning on accumulated points is victory by points or technical superiority, which is different from a fall.

question: Which Indian wrestler won a bronze medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, ending India's 56-year wait for an Olympic medal in wrestling?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sushil Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sushil Kumar won a bronze medal in the 66 kg freestyle category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. It was India's first Olympic medal in wrestling since 1952, ending a wait of 56 years. (सुशील कुमार — 2008 बीजिंग ओलंपिक, कुश्ती कांस्य)

 

• He went on to win a silver at the London 2012 Olympics, becoming the first Indian to win two individual Olympic medals in independent India. He also won gold at the 2010 World Wrestling Championships, the only Indian to have done so.

 

• India's very first individual Olympic medal was won by the wrestler K.D. Jadhav, who took bronze at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.

 

• At the same Beijing 2008 Games, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold in the 10 m air rifle, and Vijender Singh won a bronze in boxing, defeating Carlos Góngora of Ecuador in the quarter-final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other Olympic wrestling medallists: Yogeshwar Dutt (bronze, London 2012), Sakshi Malik (bronze, Rio 2016 — the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal), Ravi Dahiya (silver) and Bajrang Punia (bronze) at Tokyo 2020, and Aman Sehrawat (bronze) at Paris 2024.

 

• The Wrestling Federation of India is the national governing body, and the Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav Award of Maharashtra honours the pioneer of Indian Olympic wrestling.

 

NOTE

 

• Yogeshwar Dutt (Option 1): Won bronze at London 2012, not Beijing.

 

• Bajrang Punia (Option 2) and Ravi Dahiya (Option 3): Both won their Olympic medals at Tokyo 2020.

question: The permanent Secretariat of BIMSTEC, of which India is a founding member, is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhaka, Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The permanent Secretariat of BIMSTEC was established at Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 2014. (बिम्सटेक सचिवालय — ढाका, बांग्लादेश)

 

• BIMSTEC stands for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation. It was formed in 1997 by the Bangkok Declaration, originally as BIST-EC.

 

• It has seven member states — Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand — thus linking five countries of South Asia with two of South East Asia, and serving as a bridge between the two regions.

 

• BIMSTEC has gained importance for India as an alternative to SAARC, whose summits have been suspended, and it complements India's "Neighbourhood First" and "Act East" policies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SAARC Secretariat is at Kathmandu, Nepal. SAARC was founded in 1985 at Dhaka and has eight members, BIMSTEC's seven minus Myanmar and Thailand, plus Pakistan, Afghanistan and the Maldives.

 

• Financial cooperation mechanisms in the region include the SAARC Currency Swap Framework, operationalised by India for the 2024-27 period to provide short-term foreign exchange liquidity support to member countries and so strengthen regional financial resilience, and the SAARC Development Fund, based at Thimphu.

 

• Other groupings: IORA (Indian Ocean Rim Association), with its secretariat at Ebene, Mauritius, and the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathmandu, Nepal (Option 2): Hosts the SAARC Secretariat.

 

• Colombo, Sri Lanka (Option 3): Hosts the Indian Ocean Conference and the Colombo Security Conclave, but not BIMSTEC.

 

• Bangkok, Thailand (Option 4): The city where BIMSTEC was founded in 1997 by the Bangkok Declaration, but not the seat of its Secretariat.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

The Sports Authority of India (SAI), the apex national sports body under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, was established in the year ______, to make use of the infrastructure created for the 1982 Asian Games.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1984.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sports Authority of India (SAI) was set up in 1984 as a registered society under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, with its headquarters at New Delhi. (भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण — 1984 में स्थापित)

 

• Its immediate purpose was to make productive use of the stadia and infrastructure created for the 1982 Asian Games held in New Delhi, and its wider mandate is the broad-basing of sport and the promotion of excellence among Indian athletes.

 

• In 1987 the Society for National Institutes of Physical Education and Sports (SNIPES) was merged with SAI, bringing under it the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS), Patiala, and the Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education, Thiruvananthapuram.

 

• SAI runs the national coaching scheme, the National Centres of Excellence, the SAI Training Centres, and the Khelo India infrastructure across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Institute of Sports was established in 1961 in the former palace of the Maharaja of Patiala, and was renamed the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) on 23 January 1973, the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. It is India's premier institute for the training of coaches.

 

• Other landmarks: the Indian Olympic Association was founded in 1927; Khelo India began in 2018; the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) in 2014; and the National Sports Governance Act was enacted in 2025.

 

NOTE

 

• 1982 (Option 1): The year of the New Delhi Asian Games, whose infrastructure SAI was created to manage — but SAI itself came two years later.

 

• 1986 (Option 3) and 1990 (Option 4) are incorrect; SAI was already functioning by then, and SNIPES merged with it in 1987.

question:
Consider the following statements about "The God of Small Things" by Arundhati Roy:

1) It won the Booker Prize in 1997.

2) It is set largely in Ayemenem in Kerala.

3) It is a work of non-fiction on India's environmental movements.

Which of the following is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statements 1 and 2 both are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. 'The God of Small Things' (1997) won the Booker Prize in 1997. It was Arundhati Roy's debut novel, and she became the first Indian woman to win the prize. (द गॉड ऑफ स्मॉल थिंग्स — 1997 बुकर पुरस्कार)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The novel is set largely in the village of Ayemenem in Kerala, and follows the fraternal twins Estha and Rahel, exploring caste, forbidden love and "the Love Laws" that lay down "who should be loved, and how, and how much".

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. It is a work of fiction, not non-fiction. Arundhati Roy has separately written extensively on environmental and political issues in essay collections such as 'The Algebra of Infinite Justice' and 'The End of Imagination', but the novel itself is not such a work.

 

• Her second novel is 'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' (2017).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'The Vine of Desire' (2002) by Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni explores the cultural conflicts within an Indian immigrant family across generations; it is neither a historical account of the freedom struggle nor a work of science fiction. Her other novels include 'The Mistress of Spices', 'Sister of My Heart' and 'The Palace of Illusions', a retelling of the Mahabharata from Draupadi's point of view.

 

• Indian-origin winners of the Booker Prize are V.S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006) and Aravind Adiga (2008).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect. Option 1 omits Statement 2, which is accurate; Options 3 and 4 include Statement 3, which wrongly describes a celebrated novel as non-fiction.

question:
Which statements accurately describe the water bodies of the Thar Desert region?

1. The Luni is the only large river of the region.

2. Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is a freshwater lake.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Luni is the only large river of the Thar Desert region. It rises in the Aravalli range near Ajmer, flows south-west through Rajasthan and drains into the Rann of Kachchh. Its upper course is called the Sagarmati, and its water becomes saline below Balotra — which is why it is also called the *Lavanavari* or salt river. (लूनी — थार मरुस्थल की एकमात्र बड़ी नदी)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect. Sambhar Lake, near Jaipur, is India's largest inland saltwater (saline) lake, not a freshwater lake. It is a major source of common salt and is a Ramsar site, important for migratory flamingos.

 

• Most streams of the desert are ephemeral: they appear only during the rains and disappear into the sand without reaching the sea, so the drainage is largely inland (endorheic).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Thar or Great Indian Desert lies mostly in western Rajasthan, extending into Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab, and into Pakistan. It is separated from the rest of Rajasthan by the Aravalli range, one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, whose highest peak is Guru Shikhar on Mount Abu.

 

• Important lakes of Rajasthan: the saline lakes Sambhar, Didwana, Pachpadra and Lunkaransar, and the freshwater lakes Jaisamand (the largest artificial freshwater lake in India), Rajsamand, Pichola, Ana Sagar and Nakki.

 

• India's largest saltwater lagoon is Chilika in Odisha, and its largest freshwater lake is Wular in Jammu and Kashmir.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because Statement 1 is factually accurate while Statement 2 is not — Sambhar is a saline lake, and one of the most important sources of salt in India.

question:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): Census data is used to determine the delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies in India.

Reason (R): The Census of India is conducted once every five years.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. Census data is the basis for the delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies. Article 82 requires that after every census, the allocation of seats and the division of each State into territorial constituencies be readjusted by a Delimitation Commission constituted by Parliament. (जनगणना आँकड़े — परिसीमन का आधार)

 

• Reason (R) is false. The Census of India is conducted once every ten years (decennially), not every five years. The first synchronous census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon, and censuses have followed at ten-year intervals since.

 

• Census figures are also used for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for the devolution of funds by the Finance Commission, and for planning and policy generally.

 

• By the 84th Amendment (2001) and the 87th Amendment (2003), the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among the States has been frozen on the basis of the 1971 Census until after the first census taken after 2026, so as not to penalise States that succeeded in controlling population growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, in accordance with the Census Act, 1948. Census is a Union List subject.

 

• Birth and death registration is governed by the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. Although registration is legally compulsory, coverage is still not complete or uniform across all States, which is why the Sample Registration System (SRS) is used to estimate vital rates.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 2 are incorrect: Both require R to be true, whereas the Indian census is decennial.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The Assertion is factually accurate.

question:
Which of the following awards and the fields they recognise is/are correctly paired?

1. Dadasaheb Phalke Award - Cinema

2. Jnanpith Award - Literature

3. Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize - Science and Technology

4. Major Dhyan Chand Award - Journalism
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pair 1 is correct. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest honour in cinema, instituted in 1969 by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. It is named after Dhundiraj Govind Phalke, the father of Indian cinema, and the first recipient was Devika Rani. (दादा साहब फाल्के पुरस्कार — सिनेमा)

 

• Pair 2 is correct. The Jnanpith Award, instituted in 1961 by the Bharatiya Jnanpith, is India's highest literary honour, given for outstanding contribution to literature in any of the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule. The first recipient was G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam).

 

• Pair 3 is correct. The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, instituted in 1958 by the CSIR, is India's most prestigious award in science and technology, given to scientists under the age of 45.

 

• Pair 4 is incorrect. The Major Dhyan Chand Award is given for lifetime achievement in sports and games, not journalism. It was instituted in 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's principal sports awards are the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (the highest sporting honour, renamed in 2021), the Arjuna Award for consistent outstanding performance, the Dronacharya Award for coaches, and the Major Dhyan Chand Award for lifetime achievement.

 

• The highest honour in journalism in India is the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award, and internationally the Pulitzer Prize.

 

• The Padma awards are announced on Republic Day and are given in the categories of art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, civil service and others.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 3 are incorrect: Option 1 leaves out Pair 3, which is correct, and Option 3 includes Pair 4, which is wrong.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: It includes Pair 4, which wrongly assigns the Major Dhyan Chand Award to journalism instead of sports.

question: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, commissioned into the Indian Navy in 2022, is named:
solution_text:
The correct answer is INS Vikrant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• INS Vikrant (IAC-1) is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier. It was commissioned on 2 September 2022 at Kochi, and was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited. (आईएनएस विक्रांत — भारत का पहला स्वदेशी विमानवाहक पोत)

 

• With this India joined the small group of nations — the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, France and China — capable of designing and building an aircraft carrier of this size. It has an indigenous content of about 76 per cent.

 

• The ship displaces about 45,000 tonnes, can carry roughly 30 aircraft including MiG-29K fighters and helicopters, and uses a STOBAR (Short Take-Off But Arrested Recovery) configuration with a ski-jump.

 

• It takes its name from the first INS Vikrant, India's first aircraft carrier, acquired from Britain in 1961, which played a decisive role in the 1971 India-Pakistan war. Its motto is "Jayema Sam Yudhi Sprdhah" — "I defeat those who fight against me".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Navy at present operates two aircraft carriers — INS Vikramaditya, acquired from Russia in 2013 and originally the *Admiral Gorshkov*, and INS Vikrant.

 

• INS Arihant is India's first indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), which completed India's nuclear triad. INS Viraat, decommissioned in 2017, had served the longest of any warship in the world.

 

• The 2022 commissioning of INS Vikrant also saw the unveiling of the new Naval Ensign (Nishaan), which replaced the St George's Cross with a design drawn from the seal of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

NOTE

 

• INS Vikramaditya (Option 1): Acquired from Russia; not indigenously built.

 

• INS Viraat (Option 2): Formerly HMS Hermes of the Royal Navy, acquired from Britain and decommissioned in 2017.

 

• INS Arihant (Option 3): A nuclear-powered submarine, not an aircraft carrier.

question: The term 'polygenic inheritance' refers to:
option_1: A single trait controlled by the combined effect of two or more genes
option_2: One gene producing effects on several unrelated traits
option_3: A mutation occurring in a single allele of a gene
option_4: The duplication of an entire gene within a chromosome
solution_text:
The correct answer is A single trait controlled by the combined effect of two or more genes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Polygenic inheritance is the pattern in which a single trait is governed by two or more genes, each contributing a small additive effect. The result is a continuous range of variation rather than sharply distinct categories. (बहुजीनी वंशागति — एक लक्षण, अनेक जीन)

 

• Classic examples in human beings are skin colour, height, eye colour, body weight and intelligence, all of which vary continuously across a population and are also influenced by the environment.

 

• The exact opposite concept is pleiotropy, in which one gene affects several different and apparently unrelated traits. A standard example is sickle-cell anaemia, where a single mutation in the haemoglobin gene affects the shape of red blood cells, oxygen transport, spleen function and resistance to malaria.

 

• Related terms: codominance, where both alleles express themselves fully, as in the AB blood group; incomplete dominance, as in the pink flowers of a four o'clock plant; and multiple alleles, as in the ABO blood group system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gregor Johann Mendel, the "Father of Genetics", worked on the garden pea (Pisum sativum) and gave the Law of Dominance, the Law of Segregation and the Law of Independent Assortment.

 

• The term "gene" was coined by Wilhelm Johannsen and "genetics" by William Bateson. DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms, and a gene is the segment of DNA that codes for a particular protein.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: One gene affecting several traits is pleiotropy, the converse of polygenic inheritance.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: A change in a single allele is a point mutation.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The copying of a gene within a chromosome is gene duplication, a form of chromosomal mutation.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the position of the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in an Indian State?
option_1: Its members are directly elected by the people of the State
option_2: It enjoys powers equal to those of the Legislative Assembly in respect of all Bills
option_3: It can be created or abolished by Parliament, if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority
option_4: Once created, it can be abolished only by a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368
solution_text:
The correct answer is It can be created or abolished by Parliament, if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 169, Parliament may create or abolish a Legislative Council in a State, provided the Legislative Assembly of that State first passes a resolution by a special majority — that is, a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. (अनुच्छेद 169 — विधान परिषद का सृजन एवं उत्समापन)

 

• Such a law is not deemed to be a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368 and can be passed by a simple majority in Parliament. India therefore has an asymmetrical bicameralism: only a few States have Councils.

 

• The Council is a partly elected, partly nominated continuing chamber which is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, and members hold office for six years. Its strength must not exceed one-third of the strength of the Assembly, and must not be less than 40.

 

• Its composition: 1/3 elected by members of local bodies, 1/3 by the members of the Legislative Assembly, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, and the remaining 1/6 nominated by the Governor from persons with special knowledge of literature, science, art, the cooperative movement and social service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Legislative Council is a subordinate chamber. It can delay an Ordinary Bill by a maximum of four months (three months in the first instance and one month in the second), and it has no power to reject it. There is no provision for a joint sitting at the State level.

 

• On a Money Bill, the powers of the Rajya Sabha and the State Legislative Councils are alike restricted: they may only make recommendations, and must return the Bill within fourteen days, after which it is deemed passed.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Members of the Council are indirectly elected or nominated; only the Legislative Assembly is directly elected.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The Council's powers are distinctly weaker than those of the Assembly.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Abolition requires only an ordinary law of Parliament under Article 169, not a constitutional amendment.

question: The recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired from it is the best illustration of which of the following?
option_3: The law of conservation of energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newton's third law of motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's third law of motion states that to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, and that the two act on different bodies. (न्यूटन का गति का तृतीय नियम — क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया)

 

• When a gun is fired, the gun exerts a forward force on the bullet (action), and the bullet exerts an equal and opposite backward force on the gun (reaction), which is felt as recoil. The same law also follows from the conservation of linear momentum: the forward momentum of the light bullet equals the backward momentum of the heavy gun, so the gun moves back with a much smaller velocity.

 

• Other everyday illustrations of the third law: the walking of a person, who pushes the ground backwards while the ground pushes him forward; the motion of a rocket, which expels gases downwards; the swimming of a person; and the backward movement of a boat when one steps off it.

 

• Newton's first law (the law of inertia) explains why a heavy box is difficult to start moving and also difficult to stop once moving — that is the property of inertia, which is measured by mass. Newton's second law gives F = ma and defines force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inertia is of three kinds: inertia of rest, inertia of motion and inertia of direction. A passenger falling backwards when a bus starts suddenly illustrates the inertia of rest, and falling forward when it stops suddenly illustrates the inertia of motion.

 

• Newton's laws were set out in the Principia Mathematica (1687). The SI unit of force, the newton, is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².

 

NOTE

 

• Newton's first law (Option 2): Explains inertia — a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

 

• The law of conservation of energy (Option 3): States that energy can be neither created nor destroyed, only transformed.

 

• The principle of moments (Option 4): Relates to the equilibrium of a body under turning forces, as in a lever or a see-saw.

question: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, deals with which branch of law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Procedural civil law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908, is a procedural (adjective) law. It lays down the machinery and procedure by which civil courts try suits — the institution of a suit, pleadings, issue of summons, framing of issues, trial, execution of decrees, appeals, reference, review and revision. (दीवानी प्रक्रिया संहिता, 1908 — प्रक्रियात्मक विधि)

 

• Law is broadly divided into two kinds:

◦ Substantive law — defines rights, duties and liabilities, and what constitutes an offence and its punishment. Examples: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (criminal), the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882

◦ Procedural (adjective) law — prescribes the process of enforcing those rights. Examples: the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (criminal procedure) and the Limitation Act, 1963

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, which replaced the Indian Evidence Act, is generally treated as adjective law as well, since it governs how facts are proved in court.

 

• The CPC is divided into a body of sections dealing with general principles of jurisdiction, and a set of Orders and Rules in the First Schedule dealing with the detailed method of proceeding, which the High Courts may amend.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860, consolidates and amends substantive criminal law — it defines offences and prescribes punishments.

 

• Civil law deals with disputes between private parties over rights, property and obligations, and the remedy is usually compensation or restitution; criminal law deals with wrongs against the State and the remedy is punishment.

 

• Civil Procedure, Criminal Procedure and Evidence are all subjects of the Concurrent List.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Substantive criminal law is contained in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The law of evidence is now the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Constitutional law concerns the structure and powers of the State and the rights of citizens, and is contained chiefly in the Constitution itself.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The National Green Hydrogen Mission seeks to make India a global hub for the production and export of green hydrogen.

Reason (R): Green hydrogen is produced by the electrolysis of water using electricity generated from fossil-fuel power plants.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023 with an outlay of about Rs. 19,744 crore, aims to make India a global hub for the production, use and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives. Its targets include an annual production capacity of at least 5 million metric tonnes by 2030. (राष्ट्रीय हरित हाइड्रोजन मिशन, 2023)

 

• Reason (R) is false. Green hydrogen is produced by the electrolysis of water using electricity from renewable sources such as solar and wind — that is precisely what makes it "green". Hydrogen produced with fossil-fuel electricity or from natural gas is not green.

 

• The colour classification of hydrogen:

◦ Green hydrogen — electrolysis of water using renewable electricity; no carbon emissions

◦ Grey hydrogen — from natural gas by steam methane reforming, with CO₂ released to the atmosphere

◦ Blue hydrogen — from fossil fuels, but with carbon capture and storage

◦ Brown or black hydrogen — from coal gasification

 

• The Mission is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), not by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Green hydrogen is valued as a means of decarbonising "hard-to-abate" sectors — refining, fertilizers, steel, cement, shipping and long-haul transport — where direct electrification is difficult.

 

• Components of the Mission include the SIGHT programme (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition), which incentivises electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production, together with green hydrogen hubs, pilot projects and support for research.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 2 are incorrect: Both require R to be true, whereas the defining feature of green hydrogen is the use of renewable, not fossil-fuel, electricity.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The Assertion is factually accurate.

question:
Fill in the Blank:

The Karma dance, performed by the tribal communities of central and eastern India, is associated with the worship of the ______ tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Karma (Karam) dance is performed during the Karma festival, which centres on the worship of the Karam tree, regarded as the symbol of good fortune, fertility and prosperity. (करमा नृत्य — करम वृक्ष की पूजा)

 

• A branch of the Karam tree is ceremonially brought and planted in the village courtyard, and men and women dance around it through the night in concentric circles, arms linked, to the beat of the mandar drum and the timki.

 

• The festival is celebrated on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada (August-September), chiefly in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, by the Oraon, Munda, Baiga, Gond and other communities. Sisters observe it for the wellbeing of their brothers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian folk dances associated with particular communities or occupations:

◦ Koli — Maharashtra, performed by the fisherfolk community, its movements imitating the rowing of boats and the casting of nets

◦ Dhangari Gaja — Maharashtra, of the shepherd community

◦ Kalbelia — Rajasthan, of the snake-charmer community, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage

◦ Gaur Maria — Chhattisgarh, of the Maria Gond tribe

◦ Santhali (Sohrai) — Jharkhand and West Bengal, of the Santhal tribe

◦ Bhavai — Rajasthan and Gujarat, involving balancing pots on the head

 

• The Jawa festival, associated with Karma, is one in which unmarried girls sow grain in small baskets and offer green melons, a rite symbolising the desire for a son and fertility.

 

NOTE

 

• Peepal (Option 1): Held sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism — the Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal (bodhi) tree — but it is not the tree of the Karma festival.

 

• Banyan (Option 3): The national tree of India, worshipped during Vat Savitri.

 

• Mahua (Option 4): Economically vital to tribal communities for its flowers and oil, but not the tree venerated in the Karma dance.

question: The 'World Investment Report', which tracks trends in global foreign direct investment, is published annually by which organisation?
option_3: The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Investment Report (WIR) has been published annually since 1991 by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). It analyses trends in foreign direct investment (FDI) worldwide and its implications for development. (विश्व निवेश रिपोर्ट — अंकटाड)

 

• UNCTAD was established in 1964 as a permanent intergovernmental body of the United Nations General Assembly, and is headquartered at Geneva, Switzerland. Its purpose is to help developing countries participate equitably in the global economy.

 

• UNCTAD also publishes the Trade and Development Report, the Technology and Innovation Report and the Digital Economy Report.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major international reports and their publishers:

◦ World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report — IMF

◦ World Development Report and Logistics Performance Index — World Bank

◦ World Trade Report — WTO

◦ Human Development Report — UNDP

◦ Global Energy Transition Index and the Global Competitiveness, Global Gender Gap and Global Risks Reports — World Economic Forum

◦ World Employment and Social Outlook — ILO

◦ State of the World's Children — UNICEF

◦ World Energy Outlook — International Energy Agency (IEA)

◦ World Energy Transitions Outlook — IRENA

 

NOTE

 

• The IMF (Option 1): Established at Bretton Woods in 1944 and headquartered at Washington D.C., it deals with monetary cooperation and balance-of-payments support.

 

• The World Bank (Option 2): Also a Bretton Woods institution at Washington D.C., it provides development finance.

 

• The WTO (Option 4): Founded in 1995, successor to the GATT, headquartered at Geneva; it deals with the rules of international trade rather than investment flows.

question: In the Indian economy, 'disguised unemployment' is most commonly associated with which sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Disguised unemployment is a situation in which more people are engaged in work than are actually required, so that the marginal productivity of the additional workers is zero or nearly zero. If some of them were withdrawn, total output would not fall. (प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गारी — कृषि क्षेत्र)

 

• It is most characteristic of Indian agriculture, where an entire family may work on a small holding that could be managed by far fewer hands. The workers appear to be employed, but their contribution to output is negligible — which is why it is also called hidden unemployment.

 

• Other important types of unemployment:

◦ Seasonal unemployment — work available only in certain seasons, again common in agriculture and in the sugar industry

◦ Structural unemployment — arising from a mismatch between the skills of workers and the requirements of the economy

◦ Frictional unemployment — the short-term unemployment of people moving between jobs

◦ Cyclical unemployment — caused by a downturn in the business cycle

◦ Educated unemployment — qualified persons unable to find suitable work

◦ Open unemployment — persons willing and able to work but with no work at all

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Data on employment and unemployment in India come from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by the National Statistical Office since 2017-18, which replaced the earlier quinquennial NSSO employment surveys.

 

• Government responses to rural underemployment include the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, which guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

 

NOTE

 

• Information technology (Option 2) and Banking and insurance (Option 3): Both belong to the services sector, where employment is largely formal and productivity per worker is high.

 

• Mining and quarrying (Option 4): Employment here is generally capital-intensive and regulated, and it does not display the surplus-labour pattern typical of agriculture.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

Article 32 of the Constitution, described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the "heart and soul of the Constitution", guarantees the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies — the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the "heart and soul of the Constitution", without which the Constitution would be a nullity. (अनुच्छेद 32 — संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार)

 

• Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, and it cannot be suspended except during a National Emergency, as provided by Article 359.

 

• Under it the Supreme Court may issue five writs:

◦ Habeas Corpus — "to have the body"; against unlawful detention

◦ Mandamus — "we command"; to compel a public authority to perform its duty

◦ Prohibition — issued by a higher court to a lower court to stop exceeding its jurisdiction

◦ Certiorari — "to be certified"; to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal

◦ Quo Warranto — "by what authority"; against the usurper of a public office

 

• Article 226 gives the High Courts a wider writ jurisdiction, since they may issue writs both for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose — that is, for ordinary legal rights as well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The six Fundamental Rights at present are the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), the Right to Freedom (19-22), the Right against Exploitation (23-24), the Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30) and the Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

 

• The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment, 1978, and is now a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.

 

NOTE

 

• The Right to Equality (Option 1): Articles 14 to 18.

 

• The Right against Exploitation (Option 2): Articles 23 and 24, which prohibit trafficking, forced labour and the employment of children below 14 in hazardous work.

 

• The Right to Freedom of Religion (Option 3): Articles 25 to 28.

question: Which national park in India is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gir National Park, Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, in the Junagadh, Gir Somnath and Amreli districts of Gujarat, is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) left in the world. (गिर राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — एशियाई सिंह का एकमात्र प्राकृतिक आवास)

 

• The Asiatic Lion once ranged from West Asia across to eastern India, but was reduced to a handful of animals in Gir by the early twentieth century, and was saved largely through the protection given by the Nawab of Junagadh. Gir was declared a sanctuary in 1965 and a national park in 1975.

 

• The Asiatic Lion is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is placed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The Asiatic Lion Conservation Project was launched in 2018, and a lion census is conducted every five years.

 

• The lion is smaller than its African cousin and has a distinctive longitudinal fold of skin along the belly, and the males have a less developed mane.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important national parks and their flagship species:

◦ Kaziranga (Assam) — the one-horned rhinoceros; a UNESCO World Heritage Site

◦ Kanha and Bandhavgarh (Madhya Pradesh) — tigers; Kanha is also home to the barasingha (swamp deer)

◦ Bandipur and Nagarhole (Karnataka) — tigers and elephants

◦ Keoladeo (Rajasthan) — migratory birds, a Ramsar site and World Heritage Site

◦ Dachigam (Jammu and Kashmir) — the hangul or Kashmir stag

◦ Manas (Assam) — the golden langur and pygmy hog

◦ Sundarbans (West Bengal) — the Royal Bengal Tiger in mangroves

 

• India's first national park was Hailey National Park, established in 1936 and now called Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand, where Project Tiger was launched in 1973.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanha (Option 1) and Bandipur (Option 2): Tiger reserves under Project Tiger; lions are not found there in the wild.

 

• Kaziranga (Option 3): Famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, not the lion.

question: Which gas constitutes the largest proportion of the Earth's atmosphere by volume?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, forming about 78.08 per cent by volume of dry air. (नाइट्रोजन — वायुमंडल का लगभग 78%)

 

• The composition of dry air by volume:

◦ Nitrogen — 78.08%

◦ Oxygen — 20.95% (roughly 21%)

◦ Argon — 0.93%

◦ Carbon dioxide — about 0.04%

◦ Trace gases — neon, helium, krypton, xenon, hydrogen, ozone and methane

 

• Nitrogen is relatively inert and acts as a diluent, moderating the rate of combustion and oxidation; it becomes available to plants through nitrogen fixation by bacteria and by lightning. Oxygen is essential for respiration and combustion. Argon is the most abundant noble gas in the atmosphere.

 

• Carbon dioxide, though present in a very small proportion, is vital because it is used in photosynthesis and is a major greenhouse gas that traps outgoing terrestrial radiation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Water vapour varies greatly, from almost nothing over deserts and the poles to about 4 per cent in the humid tropics, and is not counted in the composition of "dry air".

 

• About 99 per cent of the total mass of the atmosphere lies within the lowest 32 km, and the atmosphere as a whole extends to several thousand kilometres.

 

• Greenhouse gases in order of contribution include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, chlorofluorocarbons and water vapour; methane has a far higher warming potential per molecule than carbon dioxide.

 

NOTE

 

• Oxygen (Option 1): The second most abundant gas, at about 21 per cent.

 

• Carbon dioxide (Option 3): Present in only about 0.04 per cent, though critical for climate and plant life.

 

• Argon (Option 4): About 0.93 per cent; the most abundant of the noble gases in air.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Supreme Court exercises the power of judicial review over laws made by Parliament and the State Legislatures.

2. The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is provided for under Article 143 of the Constitution.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Supreme Court exercises the power of judicial review, and may declare a law made by Parliament or a State Legislature unconstitutional if it violates the Constitution. Judicial review flows chiefly from Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226 and 246. (न्यायिक पुनरावलोकन)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Article 143 confers advisory (consultative) jurisdiction: the President may refer to the Supreme Court any question of law or fact of public importance, or any dispute arising out of a pre-Constitution treaty or agreement. The Court may give its opinion in the first case but must do so in the second, and the opinion is not binding on the President.

 

• The Supreme Court's jurisdictions are:

◦ Original (Article 131) — federal disputes between the Centre and States or between States

◦ Writ (Article 32) — enforcement of Fundamental Rights

◦ Appellate (Articles 132-136) — constitutional, civil and criminal appeals, and special leave to appeal under Article 136

◦ Advisory (Article 143)

◦ Court of Record (Article 129) — including the power to punish for contempt

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 139A, which empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases from one High Court to another and to withdraw to itself cases involving the same questions of law pending before several High Courts, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 

• Famous advisory references under Article 143 include the Delhi Laws Act case (1951), the Kerala Education Bill (1958), the Presidential Reference on the Berubari Union (1960), the Special Courts Bill (1978), the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal reference (1992) and the 2G spectrum reference (2012).

 

• The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950; its strength is currently 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.
